report.headline: EuroLeague high-usage playmaker projected for a usage rate near NBA average, with the shot-efficiency projection carrying no real signal

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to fall from 26.6% in the EuroLeague to 19.9% in the NBA, landing almost exactly at the league average of 20.1%; the 80% interval (14.2%-25.5%) spans about two standard deviations of NBA usage (5.6%).

risks.text: Usage is projected to drop by roughly 6.7 percentage points, from 26.6% to 19.9%, shrinking the shot-creation role from well above EuroLeague average to right at NBA average.

True shooting is projected to decline from 59.1% to 56.3%, below the NBA average of 58.1%, though this projection is unreliable since the model does not beat a simple league-mean baseline on this metric.
The 95% usage interval (11.2%-28.5%) is wide enough that an individual outcome could land far from the point projection.
A 16.8% turnover rate accompanies the high assist responsibility (29.3% assist rate), a combination that could carry more risk under NBA pace and spacing.

strengths.text: Strong playmaking profile in the source season: a 29.3% assist rate and 6.162 assists per 75 possessions.
Efficient scoring for the shot-creation load carried: a 59.1% true shooting percentage on 26.6% usage, almost exactly at the EuroLeague average (+0.01 sd).
Heavy three-point reliance in shot selection, with 56.8% of attempts coming from three.
Sat well above the typical mover in usage standing (+1.26 sd within the EuroLeague), compared to the +0.46 sd average for players who make this move historically.

uncertainty.text: The usage projection is a rank estimate, not a point estimate: its 80% interval (14.2%-25.5%) and 95% interval (11.2%-28.5%) cover most of the plausible NBA usage range given a league standard deviation of 5.6%. The true-shooting model's own error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league mean (also 4.7%), so its 56.3% projection should be treated as uninformative rather than as a forecast.
